description: Whether the frontend finds what each catalogue entry launches, and where (#84): whole fixture machines in, each entry's availability, launcher and core_path out, with the one reason caveat each verdict other than startable carries — asserted with exact equality through the same contract serializations as every family.

vectors.name: launch-a-standalone-component-is-found-where-the-sandbox-holds-it
vectors.rationale: Dolphin's find rules end in RetroDECK's component launcher, an /app path: atlas reads it out of the running deploy, so the entry is startable and its launcher is the sandbox spelling with the app id it is valid in. The flatpak exports entry before it never hits, though the host has that file — flatpak binds none of the host's /var into the sandbox.

vectors.name: launch-a-missing-core-is-not-installed
vectors.rationale: RetroArch is found and no corepath directory holds the core, so ES-DE refuses the launch: not-installed, with core-not-installed naming the core file and the corepath entries searched. The NixOS entry under /run is one flatpak never shows the sandbox, so it is a miss — the host's copy of the core there included — rather than a path atlas cannot tell.

vectors.name: launch-tilde-is-the-config-home-the-frontend-gets-not-the-real-home
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK starts ES-DE with --home ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}, so ~ in a find rule is the app's config directory. FOO's AppImage under that ~/Applications is found; BAR's sits only in the user's real ~/Applications, which ES-DE never looks in, so BAR is not-installed.

vectors.name: launch-a-glob-takes-the-first-match-in-sorted-order
vectors.rationale: A * takes the first file the sorted directory listing matches: Foo-1.0 before Foo-2.0, whatever order the directory lists them in.

vectors.name: launch-a-dead-symlink-counts-as-found

vectors.name: launch-a-pipe-entry-carries-its-replacement-command

vectors.name: launch-no-rules-for-the-token-is-unestablished

vectors.name: launch-an-override-that-sets-filesystems-makes-a-host-path-unestablished
vectors.rationale: An overrides file that sets filesystems at all may have revoked or widened the metadata's host grant, and atlas does not compose those grants: a host path is then unestablished, while the app's own ~/.var/app tree, where ~ points, is still read.

vectors.name: launch-the-sandboxs-private-run-user-is-unestablished
vectors.rationale: /run/user in the sandbox is its private runtime directory, not the host's, so a rule entry there is a path atlas cannot tell about.

vectors.name: launch-another-apps-flatpak-dir-is-masked-in-the-sandbox
vectors.rationale: Flatpak hides the rest of ~/.var/app and the user's Flatpak installation from the sandbox, so a rule entry naming another app's tree or the user's exports is a miss even where the file is there on the host.

vectors.name: launch-the-hosts-usr-under-run-host-is-found-under-the-host-grant
vectors.rationale: Under the host grant flatpak binds the host's /usr at /run/host/usr, so a rule entry there is the host's own file: found, and the launcher keeps the sandbox spelling ES-DE checked.

vectors.name: launch-a-merged-usr-directory-under-run-host-follows-the-hosts-own-link
vectors.rationale: /run/host/bin is recreated the way the host has it, an absolute link into /usr made relative: the host's /bin links to /usr/bin, so /run/host/bin/foo is the host's /usr/bin/foo, not the runtime's.

vectors.name: launch-run-host-without-the-host-grant-is-not-there
vectors.rationale: Without a host, host-os or host-etc grant flatpak binds nothing at /run/host, so a rule entry there misses even where the host has the file: not-installed.

vectors.name: launch-an-explicit-grant-in-the-metadata-is-a-host-read
vectors.rationale: The metadata grants another app's tree (~/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam, as RetroDECK's does), which flatpak binds over the mask it puts on the rest of ~/.var/app: a rule entry there is found.

vectors.name: launch-a-relative-path-entry-is-unestablished
vectors.rationale: An overridden PATH with a relative directory makes ES-DE test bin/foo against its own working directory, which is nothing atlas can read on this disk: the walk stops there, unestablished with that path.

vectors.name: launch-a-relative-staticpath-is-unestablished
vectors.rationale: A staticpath entry with no leading / or ~ is a path relative to ES-DE's working directory: unestablished with that path, not a miss.

vectors.name: launch-a-grant-above-a-masked-tree-does-not-lift-the-mask
vectors.rationale: The metadata grants ~/.local/share, but flatpak puts its tmpfs over the user's own Flatpak installation after the grants, and a parent's bind does not reach beneath it: a rule entry under ~/.local/share/flatpak/exports misses, the host's file there included.

vectors.name: launch-a-grant-above-another-apps-tree-does-not-lift-its-mask
vectors.rationale: A grant of ~/.var is above the tmpfs flatpak puts on ~/.var/app, so another app's tree stays masked: a rule entry there misses.

vectors.name: launch-a-grant-flatpak-refuses-binds-nothing
vectors.rationale: flatpak refuses to export anything under /etc, so a metadata grant of /etc/emus binds nothing: the sandbox's /etc is the runtime's and flatpak's, which atlas does not read, so the entry is unestablished.

vectors.name: launch-a-refused-grant-under-run-host-leaves-the-host-grants-binding
vectors.rationale: A grant of /run/host/usr is one flatpak refuses; /run/host/usr is still the host's /usr through the host grant, so the rule entry there is found.

vectors.name: launch-a-revoked-entry-in-the-metadata-hides-its-tree
vectors.rationale: A negated entry in the metadata is exported as a tmpfs: it hides ~/Applications from the sandbox even under the host grant, so a rule entry there misses, the host's file included.

vectors.name: launch-the-home-grant-binds-the-home-alone
vectors.rationale: With home and no host grant the sandbox sees the user's home: a rule entry there is found, while one outside it is a path atlas cannot tell about.

vectors.name: launch-an-unplaced-grant-leaves-a-masked-tree-unestablished
vectors.rationale: An xdg-documents grant names a directory the model cannot place, which might be anywhere, another app's tree included: a rule entry under ~/.var/app/<other app> is then not a miss but unestablished.

vectors.name: launch-the-host-os-grant-alone-binds-run-host-usr
vectors.rationale: host-os without host binds the host's /usr at /run/host/usr as the host grant does, so a rule entry there is found.

vectors.name: launch-a-relative-glob-is-unestablished
vectors.rationale: A relative staticpath with a * lists a directory relative to ES-DE's working directory, which atlas cannot read: unestablished with that directory, not a miss.

vectors.name: launch-a-grant-under-an-unbound-root-is-a-host-read
vectors.rationale: The host grant leaves the host's /var unbound, but a grant of /var/lib/emus binds that tree, and flatpak creates the directories leading to it: a rule entry there is the host's file and is found.

vectors.name: launch-a-grant-of-run-is-refused
vectors.rationale: flatpak refuses a grant that is a parent of a path it reserves (/run/host, /run/flatpak), so a grant of /run binds nothing; the sandbox's /run is flatpak's own, the host's /run unbound under the host grant, so a rule entry there misses, the host's file included.

vectors.name: launch-a-revocation-the-model-cannot-place-leaves-host-paths-unestablished
vectors.rationale: A revoked xdg-documents names a directory the model cannot place, which might hide anything: every host path is then unestablished, so the walk stops at the first rule entry, before the component launcher the deploy holds.

vectors.name: launch-the-last-spelling-of-an-entry-wins
vectors.rationale: ~/Applications is granted and then revoked in the same metadata; flatpak keeps one spelling per entry, the last, so the tree is hidden and a rule entry there misses, the host's file included.

vectors.name: launch-a-negated-host-grants-nothing
vectors.rationale: !host is no grant: without the host grant atlas does not establish what the sandbox sees outside the app's own trees, so a host path is unestablished rather than found or missed.

vectors.name: launch-the-innermost-mask-and-the-longest-grant-decide
vectors.rationale: The metadata grants ~/.var, another app's tree under the ~/.var/app mask, and revokes one directory inside that tree. The innermost mask and the longest grant decide: Foo's entry inside the revoked directory misses, and Bar's beside it is found through the grant at the app's tree, which ~/.var alone would not lift.

vectors.name: launch-a-revocation-flatpak-refuses-masks-nothing
vectors.rationale: flatpak refuses a revocation under /etc as it refuses a grant there, so !/etc/emus masks nothing. What decides the entry is the sandbox's own /etc, the runtime's and flatpak's, which atlas does not read: the walk stops there, so the entry is unestablished, not a miss under the revoked path.

vectors.name: launch-a-revocation-of-the-root-masks-nothing
vectors.rationale: flatpak drops a revocation of / before it reaches the exports: its parse rejects / as an entry (flatpak-context.c:997-1006 @ 1.16.6) and the metadata load skips the entry it rejects (:1867-1871). Were it kept, / is a parent of every path flatpak reserves, so it would be refused and mask nothing. Under the host grant the host's file is found.

vectors.name: launch-a-revoked-file-masks-nothing
vectors.rationale: flatpak mounts a revocation's tmpfs only on a directory and skips anything else, so a revoked AppImage hides nothing: under the host grant the rule entry naming it is the host's file and is found.

vectors.name: launch-a-revoked-path-of-unread-kind-is-unestablished
vectors.rationale: Whether flatpak masks a revoked path turns on whether it is a directory. ~/Applications cannot be read here, so atlas cannot tell what the sandbox shows under it: the rule entry there is unestablished, not a miss.

vectors.name: launch-a-standalone-entry-naming-a-core-states-no-core-path
vectors.rationale: ES-DE looks for the core of any command that names one, so this standalone entry of a custom es_systems overlay, which hands RetroArch a foo.so that is no libretro core name, is startable once RetroArch and foo.so are found. core_path is stated on a libretro entry alone, so it is null here.

files./var/lib/flatpak/app/net.retrodeck.retro:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<ruleList>
    <emulator name="DOLPHIN">
        <rule type="systempath">
            <entry>dolphin-emu</entry>
        </rule>
        <rule type="staticpath">
            <entry>~/Applications/Dolphin*.AppImage</entry>
            <entry>/var/lib/flatpak/exports/bin/org.DolphinEmu.dolphin-emu</entry>
            <entry>/app/retrodeck/components/dolphin/component_launcher.sh</entry>
        </rule>
    </emulator>
    <emulator name="RETROARCH">
        <rule type="systempath">
            <entry>retroarch</entry>
        </rule>
        <rule type="staticpath">
            <entry>~/Applications/RetroArch-Linux*.AppImage</entry>
            <entry>/app/retrodeck/components/retroarch/component_launcher.sh</entry>
        </rule>
    </emulator>
    <core name="RETROARCH">
        <rule type="corepath">
            <entry>/var/config/retroarch/cores</entry>
            <entry>~/.config/retroarch/cores</entry>
            <entry>/run/current-system/sw/lib/retroarch/cores</entry>
        </rule>
    </core>
</ruleList>

vectors.name: launch-an-emudeck-entry-is-not-evaluated-yet
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck's frontend runs on the host with its own home and a find-rules layer sealed in the AppImage; this release evaluates no lookup for it, so each entry answers unestablished with launch-resolution-unsupported naming the installation.
